title: Status update & customer postmortem draft — JSON schema regression and tenant-visible output inconsistencies
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft for customer-facing status updates and a concise postmortem following the 2029-12-24 incident where a subset of hosted API customers observed malformed or truncated JSON-like structured responses (examples: missing keys, arrays turned to strings). The aim is to produce: 1) a brief status-page friendly update, 2) a follow-up technical summary for customers, 3) an FAQ and recommended customer verification steps, and 4) proposed remediation and validation timeline.

Summary (for status page):
On 2029-12-24 02:40 UTC we detected an increase in customer reports of malformed structured outputs from the Redwood Hosted API (text-generation/json-structured routes). Affected requests returned semantically-valid text but failed to meet expected JSON schema constraints (missing fields, truncated arrays). We routed traffic to a compatible model variant and applied a hotfix to serving runtime; bulk of impacted requests were restored by 2029-12-24 04:05 UTC. We are continuing an investigation into the root cause and will publish a succinct postmortem and recommended verification steps for customers.

Impact (what customers may have seen):
- Intermittent malformed JSON-like responses for generated structured outputs on the hosted API (endpoints: /v1/generate-structured, /v1/chat with structured instructions).
- Scope: ~0.6% of total token-generation volume during window; concentrated on requests with: long prefix prompts (>2k tokens), custom stop sequences that contain special control tokens, and streaming-enabled sessions.
- Duration: spike observed starting 2029-12-24 02:38 UTC, significant mitigation by 04:05 UTC, residual rate of errors reduced to baseline by 2029-12-24 06:10 UTC.

What we did (immediate mitigation):
- Automatically routed new requests from affected tenants to a verified model variant (model-id: redwood-v1-stable) that did not use the new batching kernel.
- Deployed a targeted runtime hotpatch to fix an eviction ordering bug in the KV cache path that caused special token sequences to be dropped during streaming assembly (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/829).
- Added elevated monitoring and synthetic tests for structured-output schema validation across the fleet.

Root cause (summary):
Preliminary engineering analysis indicates a regression introduced during a rollout of a new batching/kernel-selection optimization. The optimization changed micro-batching window behavior and altered the ordering of KV cache eviction in edge conditions where: 1) prefix lengths were long, and 2) stop sequences included special control tokens (e.g., "<JSON_START>"). Under those conditions, the runtime occasionally omitted or reordered tokens during streaming assembly, which caused downstream post-processing (schema enforcement layer) to emit truncated or malformed JSON.

Why it impacted structured outputs more:
- Schema-validated outputs rely on specific delimiter tokens and complete arrays/objects; small reorderings or dropped tokens convert otherwise-valid generation into invalid JSON.
- The regression manifested primarily under streaming and when the model response used multiple KV cache slices because the batching kernel changed when we compressed KV slices for throughput.

Customer-facing timeline (concise):
- 2029-12-24 02:38 UTC — First alert from synthetic monitors and customer reports in #inc-inf-7321-thread.
- 2029-12-24 02:43 UTC — Engineering paged, incident declared.
- 2029-12-24 03:00 UTC — Initial status page update posted (traffic surge; degraded structured outputs).
- 2029-12-24 03:20 UTC — Traffic routing to redwood-v1-stable started for affected tenants.
- 2029-12-24 03:50 UTC — Hotpatch roll (runtime KV eviction fix) deployed to Canary.
- 2029-12-24 04:05 UTC — Majority of affected traffic restored; continued observation.
- 2029-12-24 06:10 UTC — Residual error rate returned to baseline.
- 2029-12-25 09:00 UTC — Deeper analysis confirmed root cause; patch backported to dedicated and private runtime builds.

Customer action checklist (recommended, short):
1) If you ingest structured outputs directly, run a quick schema check against a small sample of recent responses (we recommend 50–200 responses from 2029-12-24 02:30–06:30 UTC). If you detect malformed items, see verification steps below.
2) If you use automatic replay/ingestion pipelines, consider pausing automatic acceptance of outputs and run a lightweight syntactic validator during our remediation window.
3) Contact your account team if you require a curated evidence package or replay assistance (we can provide request IDs and raw token-level artifacts for auditing).

Verification steps for customers (how to confirm a fix):
- Quick schema validator (example pseudo-check): attempt to parse outputs with your JSON parser; count parse failures; validate presence of required keys (e.g., id, items[], metadata).
- If you saw issues during the window: provide 5–10 example request IDs to CS (or attach to the Jira INF-7321) and our team will verify whether the requests hit the affected runtime and if a replay shows corrected output under the patched runtime.

Planned next steps (engineering + customer ops):
- Postmortem: concise customer-facing postmortem to be published by 2029-12-27 with root cause, detailed mitigations, and long-term safeguards.
- Backports: runtime patch will be included in the December maintenance build and backported to customer-private bundles by 2029-12-28.
- Guardrails: add streaming schema-sanity checks in the proxy layer to detect truncated outputs mid-stream and fall back to a safe-mode response for structured routes.
- Testing: expand synthetic scenarios in CI to include long prefixes, special-token stop sequences, and high-concurrency streaming paths.

FAQ (short):
Q: Which customers were affected?
A: Impact concentrated on hosted API tenants that used structured-output routes with long prefixes and streaming. We observed tenant-level variance because not all workloads exercised the particular batching pattern. If you want a tenant-specific impact summary, ask CS and we’ll produce one.

Q: Will this happen again?
A: We have implemented an immediate fix and will add multiple safeguards (canary telemetry, proxy-level schema checks, expanded CI). While no single change can eliminate all risk, the combination of fixes makes recurrence unlikely for the same root cause.

Q: Do I need to rotate keys / change configuration?
A: No. This was a runtime bug affecting response assembly; there is no evidence of data exfiltration or API key leakage.

Q: Can you replay my requests?
A: Yes — with customer consent we can replay recorded requests against the patched runtime and provide before/after outputs for verification. Please open a ticket or reply to your account contact.

Draft status-page copy (very short):
Title: Partial disruption to structured-output routes — mitigation in progress
Body: We are investigating reports of malformed structured responses for some hosted API requests. Traffic has been routed to a compatible model variant and a runtime patch is being rolled out. Customers may see intermittent schema parse errors; majority of impacted requests were resolved by 04:05 UTC. We will publish a post-incident summary when the investigation completes.

Draft customer postmortem (concise, human-facing):
We sincerely apologize for the disruption. On 2029-12-24 a runtime regression triggered malformed structured outputs for a subset of requests. The regression was caused by a change in the batching/kernel-selection path that affected KV cache eviction ordering under long-prefix + special-token stop-sequence conditions. We mitigated the problem by routing traffic away from the affected runtime and deploying a targeted patch that corrects eviction ordering. The patch has been backported and verified. Our next steps include adding proxy-level schema checks, broader synthetic coverage, and improved canary telemetry for structured-output routes. For customers who need assistance, our CS and Solutions Engineering teams can provide request-level evidence and replays.

Tone notes (for comms):
- Keep the status update concise and time-stamped.
- The postmortem should be clear, own the failure, explain impact, and list concrete remediation/guardrails.
- Offer replay and raw evidence to enterprise customers without them having to escalate.

Open questions / decisions needed from leadership: 
- Approve offering of curated evidence packages for impacted enterprise tenants (cost estimate: 1–2 engineer-days per heavy tenant).
- Approve public postmortem by 2029-12-27 (legal review: 0.5 day).

Notes to self / next edits:
- Add specific tenant examples after CS confirms permission.
- Include sanitized example malformed response and corrected response for educational material.
- Replace placeholder links with final Confluence postmortem and consolidated Jira list.

Contact and escalation:

End of draft.
